issue_context.title: PerformanceCounter exist running in Console but missing as Windows Service
issue_context.body:
<!--This is just a template - feel free to delete any and all of it and replace as appropriate.-->

### Description
I'm trying to add performance counter to my service, when run in console, I can read counter data by calling `typeperf "\SimpleCategory\*" `. However, if I install the service by following script, `typeperf` always return 0.
```powershell
sc.exe create “Sample Service” binpath="C:\Users\Administrator\source\repos\PerfCounter\PerfCounter\bin\Debug\netcoreapp3.1\PerfCounter.exe"
sc.exe start "Sample Service"
```

I can repro this by following snippet
1. PerfCounterManager.cs, register and create counters
```csharp 
namespace PerfCounter
{
    using System;
    using System.Collections.Concurrent;
    using System.Diagnostics;
    using System.Threading;

    /// <summary>
    /// Class to manage performance counters.
    /// </summary>
    public class PerfCounterManager
    {
        /// <summary>
        /// Dictionary to hold all perf counters
        /// </summary>
        private static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<string, PerformanceCounter> perfCounters = new ConcurrentDictionary<string, PerformanceCounter>();

        /// <summary>
        /// Performance category name
        /// </summary>
        private static readonly string PerformanceCounterCategory = "SimpleCategory";

        /// <summary>
        /// Performance counter  Statistics
        /// </summary>
        public static readonly string StatisticCounter = "Statistics";

        /// <summary>
        /// Initializes static members of the <see cref="PerfCounterManager" /> class.
        /// </summary>
        static PerfCounterManager()
        {
            SetupCategory();
        }

        public static void Run(CancellationToken token)
        {
            while (!token.IsCancellationRequested)
            {
                Console.WriteLine(PerfCounterManager.Increase(PerfCounterManager.StatisticCounter));
                Thread.Sleep(100);
            }
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Increase counter
        /// </summary>
        public static long Increase(string counterName)
        {
            var perfCounter = perfCounters.GetOrAdd(counterName, new PerformanceCounter(PerformanceCounterCategory, counterName, false));
            return perfCounter.Increment();
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// If the category does not exist, create the category first.
        /// </summary>
        private static void SetupCategory()
        {
            if (System.Diagnostics.PerformanceCounterCategory.Exists(PerformanceCounterCategory))
            {
                System.Diagnostics.PerformanceCounterCategory.Delete(PerformanceCounterCategory);
            }

            CounterCreationDataCollection counterDataCollection = new CounterCreationDataCollection();

            // Add the  statistic counter.
            CounterCreationData numberOfItems = new CounterCreationData
            {
                CounterName = StatisticCounter,
                CounterType = PerformanceCounterType.NumberOfItems32
            };

            counterDataCollection.Add(numberOfItems);

            try
            {
                // Create the category.
                System.Diagnostics.PerformanceCounterCategory.Create(PerformanceCounterCategory, "Simple statistics", PerformanceCounterCategoryType.SingleInstance, counterDataCollection);
            }
            catch(Exception ex)
            {
                Console.WriteLine(ex);
            }

            PerformanceCounter.CloseSharedResources();
        }
    }
}
```
2. worker.cs. Create service
```csharp
namespace PerfCounter
{
    using Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting;
    using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
    using System;
    using System.Collections.Generic;
    using System.Text;
    using System.Threading;
    using System.Threading.Tasks;

    public class Worker : BackgroundService
    {
        public Worker()
        {
        }

        protected override async Task ExecuteAsync(CancellationToken stoppingToken)
        {
            Task.Run(() => PerfCounterManager.Run(stoppingToken));
        }
    }
}
```
3. main.cs
```csharp
namespace PerfCounter
{
    using System;
    using System.Diagnostics;
    using System.IO;
    using System.Linq;
    using System.Threading.Tasks;
    using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;
    using Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting;

    /// <summary>
    /// The program.
    /// </summary>
    internal class Program
    {
        /// <summary>
        /// Gets value indicating whether service is running in console mode.
        /// </summary>
        public static bool ConsoleMode { get; private set; }

        /// <summary>
        /// Process entry point.
        /// </summary>
        /// <param name="args">Command line arguments.</param>
        /// <returns>Task representing async operation.</returns>
        public static async Task Main(string[] args)
        {
            try
            {
                string rootPath = Path.GetDirectoryName(GetModulePath());
                IHostBuilder builder = Host.CreateDefaultBuilder()
                    .ConfigureServices((hostContext, services) =>
                    {
                        services.AddHostedService<Worker>();
                    });

                await builder.UseWindowsService().Build().RunAsync().ConfigureAwait(false);
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                Console.WriteLine(ex);
            }
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Returns full path of the executing module.
        /// </summary>
        /// <returns>Executing module path.</returns>
        private static string GetModulePath()
        {
            using (Process process = Process.GetCurrentProcess())
            {
                return process.MainModule.FileName;
            }
        }
    }
}
```

One more thing may help here, When change counter category from SingleInstance to MultiInstace, `typeperf` will throw *Error: No valid counters.* And when using PerformanceMonitor instead of typeperf in MultiInstance circumstances, the counter instance is missing when running as service. 

### Configuration
- What OS and version, and what distro if applicable?
  - Tested both in window server 2016 datacenter && Windows 10 Enterprise

@wwjue I verified and its permission issue, run the console app in the administrative mode and it will run perfectly. let me know if u hit any errors

Discussed with @Anipik offline, services should be able to provide perf counter instances.  It's possible this is a namespace or permission issue.  It looks to me like the service is set to run as Local System, which would run in Session 0.  One thing to try is to run the service as the logged on user in the current session and see if that is different.  If so then investigate what's failing when run as LocalSystem service.  The provider side of the perf-counter opens a shared memory file mapping to write counter data.  That should be session-agnostic (`Global/`) 
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/230b5b167c6a47558b9adf292d4634cf41f1d797/src/libraries/System.Diagnostics.PerformanceCounter/src/System/Diagnostics/SharedPerformanceCounter.cs#L707-L709

It then will try to create or open the filemapping, and keep trying for 1.4 minutes:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/230b5b167c6a47558b9adf292d4634cf41f1d797/src/libraries/System.Diagnostics.PerformanceCounter/src/System/Diagnostics/SharedPerformanceCounter.cs#L1698-L1724

It's possible the service is stuck in this loop and would eventually fail.

review_comments: Is it possible to use the SafeHandle here and avoid calling DangerousGetHandle?

I see, we're using the shared definition which defines this as IntPtr.  It looks like we're ensuring the SafeHandle stays alive the entire method, so this should be ok.  Just better to avoid unsafe if we can.
